abilities._source: || Duration 3 -> 4 turns, 6 Nov 2026. Kyle: 'we KNOW rejuv should not be the same duration as regrowth or wild growth etc.' He was right and ours were backwards - Rejuvenation ran 4 turns while Regrowth, the long-tail spell, was tied for SHORTEST at 3, and Wild Growth, the emergency AoE, matched the blanket. Bucket: tail - the dot you open with and leave running. The window is measured, not guessed: tools/sim_class_balance.py plus a boss-multiplier run put trash fights at 2-3 turns (p90 4-5) and boss fights at 5-6 (p90 8-10), so realised damage for a dot applied on turn 1 is 2t 100%, 3t 91%, 4t 78%, 5t 66%, 6t 57% on trash. WoW's RELATIVE ordering is preserved (Wild Growth < Rejuvenation < Regrowth) rather than its absolute seconds, which belong to a game with far longer fights. PER-TICK IS HELD AT THE SHIPPED VALUE and the total scales with duration, because effect_value is the TOTAL across the duration (abilities.py:2695) - moving duration alone would thin a fixed total instead of changing the spell's strength.
_tuning: 15 Nov 2026: a quick cast (Kyle: "Speed sets next turn"), sized 0.65x for 0.85x the cost (tools/apply_cast_speeds.py)
15 Nov 2026, class pass: every rank x0.65 - it sat at 2.47x of what an ability of its level, cooldown, AoE share, cast speed and role should be (tools/fix_strong_outliers.py)
15 Nov 2026, deep dive: damage_school arcane - it had none, so it landed as generic 'magic' and no school talent (Shadow Weaving, +shadow/fire/holy damage) ever touched it
21 Nov 2026: re-sized for the quarter-mark speeds (Kyle: "Instant should lift .25 of the bar max"): instant is now 0.25 of the meter against medium's 0.75 (tools/build_cast_speeds.py)
21 Nov 2026: an over-time spell refreshes rather than stacks, so it's sized by 0.4 of its speed's time saving, not all of it (instant: 0.73x a medium one; tools/build_cast_speeds.py)
23 Nov 2026: stays instant with a 2-turn cooldown (Kyle: "We should not have damage skills that are low mana with no cooldown being instant"; tools/build_cast_speeds.py no_spam_instants)

abilities.name: Rejuvenation
abilities.description: Nature's energy restores your health over 4 turns.
abilities._source: 29 Oct 2026, Kyle: "Resto druid is designed to be a hot Healer, we need to buff its hots." READ THE INSTRUMENT NOTE IN tools/sim_role_balance.py BEFORE RE-TUNING THIS. The 94-healing-a-turn figure that prompted the request was mostly a measurement fault: the healer sim re-cast the top-priority heal every turn at the same patient, and status_effects refreshes a same-effect_id application, so every HoT was wiped one turn after it landed and credited with a single tick - then divided by casts under a per-turn label. Measured properly the spec was on 182/turn, tenth of thirteen rather than last by 2.5x, and one of only four healers that never runs dry in a 40-turn window. So this is a modest lift into the middle of the field, not the 3x the broken number argued for. Rejuvenation 144 -> 230 (36 -> 57 a turn), Regrowth 117 -> 200 (39 -> 67). Healing Touch (134) and Swiftmend left alone on purpose - the spec should stay weakest on burst and strongest on rolling HoTs, which is what makes it read as a different healer from Priest. Durations left at 4 and 3; worth noting they are the shortest HoTs in the field (Venomancer runs 10, 8 and 7, Primalist 8 and 6, Sun Cleric 6) but that is a separate design question. || Duration 4 -> 3 turns, 6 Nov 2026. Bucket: standard - the cheap blanket you keep rolling. The window is measured, not guessed: tools/sim_class_balance.py plus a boss-multiplier run put trash fights at 2-3 turns (p90 4-5) and boss fights at 5-6 (p90 8-10), so realised damage for a dot applied on turn 1 is 2t 100%, 3t 91%, 4t 78%, 5t 66%, 6t 57% on trash. WoW's RELATIVE ordering is preserved (Wild Growth < Rejuvenation < Regrowth) rather than its absolute seconds, which belong to a game with far longer fights. PER-TICK IS HELD AT THE SHIPPED VALUE and the total scales with duration, because effect_value is the TOTAL across the duration (abilities.py:2695) - moving duration alone would thin a fixed total instead of changing the spell's strength.

Requires one of those to already be active on the target. 29 Oct 2026: consumable_hot_ids listed only druid_rejuvenation, but the ability's own failure message in combat/abilities.py says "requires an active Rejuvenation or Regrowth" and the consumable_hot_ids docstring gives ["druid_rejuvenation", "druid_regrowth"] as its worked example for Swiftmend. abilities.name: Thorns
abilities.description: Sheathes the target in thorns, increasing the damage they deal.
abilities._design_note: Real WOTLK Thorns makes enemies who melee the target take Nature damage. This engine has no reflect-damage-on-being-hit mechanic at all, so Thorns has always been an approximation. DEAD UNTIL 2026-10-29, in two ways at once: the stat_mod was {'physical_damage': 0.03}, and (a) 'physical_damage' is not a stat key anything in entities/ or combat/ reads, and (b) the buff branch int()s every non-_pct key, so 0.03 truncated to 0 - the buff landed carrying {'physical_damage': 0}. Two independent reasons for it to do nothing, which is why neither was noticed. Now damage_dealt_pct 3.0, a key the engine really reads (Ability._damage_multiplier) in PERCENT POINTS, so the +3% the old value was evidently reaching for actually applies. STILL AN APPROXIMATION: a real Thorns wants a reflect mechanic, which is Kyle's call and a bigger change than this.

Gated behind the Feral talent on 6 Nov 2026. THIS ONE IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM REAL WoW: Dire Bear Form is trainer-learned at 40 in 3.3.5a and appears nowhere in the Feral tree. But druid_feral already carries a dire_bear unlock node, and druid_feral is on the no-touch list - so the choice was a live talent that deviates, or a dead 1-point node that matches. A dead node is strictly worse for the player. Gating it costs no edit to the no-touch tree at all.
